title: Kitsuden MCP Tool Reference
description: Machine-readable schema of all Kitsuden MCP tools. Designed for LLM agent consumption.

tools.name: kitsuden_list_datasets
tools.description: List all available datasets and kons with their UUIDs, slugs, and field schemas. Use this as the first call before any CRUD operation when you do not know the dataset UUID.
whenToUse: Discovering what data collections exist in the Kitsuden instance
Finding the UUID of a dataset before querying it
Checking whether a kon was successfully installed (new datasets appear)
Exploring the data model of an unfamiliar project
whenNotToUse: You already know the dataset UUID and only need records — use kitsuden_query_dataset directly
You need table-level introspection of kon SQL tables — use the kitsuden://tables resource or kitsuden_get_schema

format.description: Result format. 'auto' (default): compact JSON, TOON or TRON, whichever is shortest for this result and decodes back to the same data; _meta['kitsuden/format'] says which. 'json' forces compact JSON.

exampleConversation.userSays: What datasets do I have?
List my collections in compact format

tools.name: kitsuden_query_dataset
tools.description: Query records from a specific dataset. Respects RLS policies automatically. Supports pagination and status filtering; results come in the shortest lossless format.
whenToUse: Reading records from a JSONB dataset
Filtering by status (published, draft, archived)
Paginating through large result sets
Returning a long list to the LLM (the default 'auto' format keeps it compact)
whenNotToUse: You need to query a native SQL table owned by a kon — use kitsuden_query_table or the kon's REST endpoint
You don't know the dataset UUID — call kitsuden_list_datasets first
You need to mutate data — use insert/update/delete instead

datasetId.description: UUID of the dataset (not the slug). Obtain from kitsuden_list_datasets.

limit.description: Maximum records to return. Hard cap at 100.

status.description: Filter by status: published, draft, archived.

format.description: Result format. 'auto' (default): compact JSON, TOON or TRON, whichever is shortest for this result and decodes back to the same data; _meta['kitsuden/format'] says which. 'json' forces compact JSON.

exampleConversation.userSays: Show me all published blog posts
Get the latest 5 tasks

tools.name: kitsuden_insert_record
tools.description: Insert a new record into a dataset. The record is stored as JSONB in data_entries. Validates against the dataset schema if one is defined.
whenToUse: Creating a new entry in a JSONB dataset
Adding a blog post, task, product, or any custom entity
Seeding initial data after creating a dataset
whenNotToUse: The target is a native SQL table from a kon — use the kon's API or kitsuden_create_record
You are bulk-inserting hundreds of rows — use kitsuden_batch_operations or the import API
You only want to update an existing record — use kitsuden_update_record

data.description: Record payload matching the dataset schema.

status.description: Initial status: draft, published, or archived.

exampleConversation.userSays: Create a blog post titled 'Hello World' with content 'My first post'

tools.name: kitsuden_update_record
tools.description: Update an existing record by entry ID. Merges the provided data with the existing JSONB payload.
whenToUse: Patching specific fields of an existing record
Changing status from draft to published
Correcting data after user feedback
whenNotToUse: You don't know the entryId — query first with kitsuden_query_dataset
You want to replace the entire record — delete and re-insert
The record is in a native SQL table — use kitsuden_update_record for datasets only

entryId.description: UUID of the entry to update.

data.description: Fields to merge into the existing record.

exampleConversation.userSays: Change the title of blog post abc-123 to 'Updated Title'
Publish draft entry xyz-789

tools.name: kitsuden_delete_record
tools.description: Hard-delete a record by entry ID. This is permanent and cannot be undone.
whenToUse: User explicitly asks to remove a record
Cleaning up test data
GDPR/data-deletion requests
whenNotToUse: You are not 100% sure which record — query first and confirm with the user
You want a soft delete — use kitsuden_update_record to set status to 'archived' instead
The record is owned by a kon with cascading relations — use the kon's delete endpoint

entryId.description: UUID of the entry to delete.

exampleConversation.userSays: Delete the blog post with ID abc-123

tools.name: kitsuden_create_dataset
tools.description: Create a new JSONB dataset with a user-defined schema. Use this for custom data structures when no kon exists.
whenToUse: User needs a custom collection that no kon covers
Prototyping a new domain before building a kon
Storing configuration or metadata objects
whenNotToUse: A kon already exists for this domain — prefer kitsuden_install_kon
You need complex SQL relations (FKs, JOINs, triggers) — kons handle this better
You only need a one-off table — consider if a dataset is overkill

fields.description: Schema fields defining the dataset structure.

enableRls.description: Enable owner-only RLS by default. Always true unless user explicitly opts out.

exampleConversation.userSays: I need a dataset to store project tasks with title, priority, and due date

tools.name: kitsuden_install_kon
tools.description: Install a domain kon (pre-built module). Automatically runs migrations, registers routes, and creates datasets.
whenToUse: User wants a standard domain feature: blog, CRM, booking, courses, games, etc.
User wants admin UI, validation, and relations out of the box
You need dependencies (e.g., kon-media for image handling)
whenNotToUse: The domain is completely custom and no kon covers it — use kitsuden_create_dataset
You are in production and cannot afford migration downtime — test in staging first
The kon is already installed — check kitsuden_list_datasets first

exampleConversation.userSays: I want to add a blog to my site
Install the CRM module

tools.name: kitsuden_define_action
tools.description: Register an automation action. Triggers can be HTTP, event, cron, or agent-based. The action runs code, webhooks, or dispatches to workers.
whenToUse: User says 'when X happens, do Y'
Sending a welcome email after signup
Calling a webhook when a record status changes
Running a scheduled cleanup job
whenNotToUse: You only need a one-off worker job — use kitsuden_dispatch_worker directly
The logic is complex and better suited to a custom kon — build a kon instead
You need real-time reactive logic — use WebSockets or the realtime layer

code.description: JavaScript/TypeScript code to run in the worker sandbox.

queueName.description: Queue to dispatch to for async execution.

exampleConversation.userSays: When a user signs up, send them a welcome email

tools.name: kitsuden_enable_auth
tools.description: Enable authentication for the Kitsuden instance. Supports email/password, OAuth (Google, Discord), and API keys.
whenToUse: User wants login, signup, or user accounts
RLS policies require an authenticated user context
Installing a kon that requires auth (CRM, booking, LMS, etc.)
whenNotToUse: Auth is already enabled — check /api/health or kitsuden_list_datasets for auth_users
The project is a fully public read-only site with no user data
You only need machine-to-machine API keys — those are managed separately in Admin → API Keys

exampleConversation.userSays: Enable user authentication with email and Google

tools.name: kitsuden_dispatch_worker
tools.description: Enqueue an asynchronous background job on the Postgres queue (transactional outbox).
whenToUse: Sending emails asynchronously
Processing images, videos, or imports
Calling external webhooks without blocking the response
Running scheduled or triggered background tasks
whenNotToUse: You need the result immediately — run synchronously via kitsuden_api_request or a direct API call
Valkey is not running — the job will fail (see troubleshooting)
The payload exceeds 1 MB — use direct API or chunked upload instead

queueName.description: Queue name: 'email', 'webhooks', or a custom queue.

exampleConversation.userSays: Send a password reset email to john@example.com

tools.name: kitsuden_query_collection
tools.description: Query any collection — dataset or native table — with pagination, search and sort; results come in the shortest lossless format. No UUID needed; uses slug/table name.
whenToUse: Reading records from any collection without needing the dataset UUID
Querying native kon tables directly
Paginating or filtering results with search/sort
whenNotToUse: You need to write raw SQL — this is abstracted
You are mutating data — use create/update/delete instead

collection.description: Dataset slug or native table name.

exampleConversation.userSays: Show me all blog posts

tools.name: kitsuden_create_record
tools.description: Create a record in any collection — dataset or native table.
whenToUse: Inserting into a dataset or native table
Creating entries without knowing the dataset UUID
whenNotToUse: The collection does not exist yet
Bulk inserts — use batch API instead

exampleConversation.userSays: Create a blog post titled Hello World

tools.name: kitsuden_update_record
tools.description: Update a record in any collection — dataset or native table.
whenToUse: Patching fields on an existing record
whenNotToUse: You don't know the record ID — query first

exampleConversation.userSays: Update blog post abc-123 title to Updated

tools.name: kitsuden_delete_record
tools.description: Delete a record from any collection — dataset or native table.
whenToUse: Removing a specific record by ID
whenNotToUse: You are not sure which record — query and confirm first
You want soft delete — update status to archived instead

tools.name: kitsuden_describe_collection
tools.description: Get the schema/fields of any collection — dataset or native table. Results come in the shortest lossless format.
whenToUse: Discovering the fields of a collection before generating code
Inspecting a kon's native table structure
whenNotToUse: You only need record counts — query with limit=0 instead

tools.name: kitsuden_system_status
tools.description: Check system health: database connectivity, queue depth, memory usage, and active kons.
whenToUse: Diagnosing why a tool call failed
Monitoring system health before batch operations
whenNotToUse: You just want data — this is operational metadata

exampleConversation.userSays: Is the system healthy?

tools.name: kitsuden_generate_frontend_hook
tools.description: Generate complete, strongly-typed frontend code (React hooks, Vue composables, Svelte stores, components, forms, types) for any collection. Uses the real codegen engine.
whenToUse: User wants frontend code to query Kitsuden
Building a vibecoder MVP and need data fetching boilerplate
Creating typed hooks/components for a specific collection
whenNotToUse: The user only wants backend changes — this tool is frontend-only
The collection does not exist yet — create or install it first

collection.description: Dataset slug or kon table name, e.g. 'blog-posts' or 'games'.
